articles.title: Iranian woman moves Madras High Court wanting to know procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous visa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 30-year-old Iranian woman, reportedly born in a Zoroastrian family but forced to practice Islam in her country before converting to Christianity, has approached the Madras High Court seeking a direction to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Chennai to explain to her the procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous Visa so that she could step out of a special camp for foreigners in Tiruchi.

Pegah Ansari, daughter of Ansari Shapour, told the court that she was born and raised in a Zoroastrian family in Tehran. Claiming that all citizens at birth get registered as Muslims, irrespective of their actual religious background or personal faith, in her country; the petitioner said: “As a result, despite being born into a Zoroastrian family, I was officially recorded as a Muslim in government records.”

She went on to state: “Throughout my life in Iran, I lived under constant fear of persecution on account of my religious beliefs and personal convictions. Over time, I came to believe in and follow the teachings of Christianity. Due to the strict restrictions imposed on religious conversion in Iran, I was compelled to practice and profess my Christian faith only in private and in secrecy.”

Ms. Ansari said, she had no other option but to flee her country in 2019 because her private conversion to Christianity came to the notice of the authorities in Iran where she faced a genuine and imminent threat of persecution, harassment and possible arrest. She flew first to Georgia and underwent conversion through appropriate religious process. She resided there till 2022.

Her second stop was Sri Lanka where stayed approximately for a month before flying down to India on a one-month-long tourist visa in April 2022. “I came to India in search of safety, stability, and the freedom to live without fear of religious persecution,” the petitioner said and claimed to have obtained refugee status from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in March 2025.

She said, the Anjugramam police in Kanniyakumari district had arrested her on December 10, 2025 when she had gone to a resort over there for decorating the venue of a birthday party. The charge levelled against her was that she had overstayed in India despite the expiry of her tourist visa on May 12, 2022. The police personnel also found that the petitioner’s Iranian passport had expired on February 17, 2024.

The petitioner was lodged at the women’s prison at Puzhal near Chennai until the Kanniyakumari Principal District and Sessions Court granted her bail on January 29, 2026. Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to the Tiruchi special camp for foreigners on the basis of a December 23, 2025 Government Order which authorised her detention in the camp until the disposal of the criminal case or her deportation.

Claiming that the State could not curtail her free movement even after grant of bail, the petitioner said, she would be able to approach the appropriate authorities for getting relocated to some other country only if she was allowed to move freely without being confined to the boundaries of the special camp. The petitioner wanted to know the procedure for obtaining the visa required to face court proceedings.
The petitioner said that she had made a representation in this regard to the FRRO on June 25, 2026 but complained that the officer did not respond.

articles.title: Ladakh administration asks activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife to stop ‘unauthorised activities’ at their Leh school
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Ladakh administration on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) asked the Himalayan Institute of Alternatives, Ladakh’s (HIAL) Desert Flower School, run by activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife, “to stop unauthorised activities of the school”, citing the matter pertaining to the allotment of land as “sub judice”. Meanwhile, Mr. Wangchuk extends support to people of Arunachal Pradesh resisting the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project.

“Desert Flower School of the HIAL Ecosystem has commenced functioning of the school without necessary clearance/approval from the competent authority. The administration asks HIAL to strictly maintain the status quo and avoid causing any prejudice to the case pending before the High Court of J&K and Ladakh,” said a spokesman of the L-G administration.

It claimed that the school “commenced activities without obtaining the requisite consent, clearances and approvals from the concerned authorities”. The administration pointed out that the matter concerning HIAL was pending adjudication before the court.

On September 22, Gitanjali Angmo, wife of Mr. Wangchuk, requested the Deputy Commissioner, Leh, for the issuance of a No Objection Certificate and clearance for the proposed members of the Managing Committee of the school located at Phyang, Leh. The Administration had cancelled the land allotment to HIAL in August 2025.

“Accordingly, the notice issued by Tehsildar, Leh, has strongly advised HIAL to maintain strict status quo and not undertake any action whatsoever towards the functioning or commencement of activities,” said the L-G order.

Meanwhile, Mr. Wangchuk, who has been campaigning for a special status for Ladakh and was jailed last year under the National Security Act (NSA), on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) wrote a letter to President Droupadi Murmu and appealed for intervention “to protect the rights of indigenous communities, democratic freedoms, and the fragile Himalayan ecology in Arunachal Pradesh”.

“I write to you with a heavy heart, as an environmental activist from Ladakh who has spent decades working to protect our fragile Himalayan environment. I urgently seek your intervention in the disturbing situation unfolding in the Siang Valley of Arunachal Pradesh, where indigenous communities, particularly the Adi people, are resisting the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. We in Ladakh understand their pain,” reads the letter.

Mr. Wangchuk said for years, people of Ladakh have been peacefully demanding constitutional safeguards under the Sixth Schedule to protect fragile ecology, ancestral lands and cultural identity. “We know what it feels like when decisions affecting our future are taken without adequately consulting us. Coming from an indigenous tribal community yourself, you understand that for us, nature is not merely a resource to be exploited, but a mother to be protected,” the letter reads.

In the letter, Mr. Wancghuk highlighted the reports about thousands of security personnel being deployed, young activists arrested, and villagers subjected to intimidation and restrictions on movement.

“There are serious allegations of police excesses, including against elderly villagers, and criminal cases against those opposing the project. What pains me particularly is the attempt to portray people raising legitimate concerns as anti-national or foreign-funded,” said Mr. Wangchuk.

He said it was deeply unfortunate that people who have stood by the nation in its most difficult times should face such accusations. “We have witnessed such allegations in Ladakh over the past year, and now similar accusations are being made against the people of Arunachal Pradesh. Such shortsighted accusations, particularly when made without credible evidence, do not strengthen national security. They weaken it. In sensitive border regions, the trust, goodwill and active cooperation of local communities are among our country’s greatest strategic strengths,” said Mr. Wangchuk.
He also appealed for de-escalation, protection of democratic rights and biological safeguards.

articles.title: SIT report says charges against KSU activists in Veena George case cannot be sustained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has submitted its final report to the court, stating that the charges levelled against Kerala Students Union (KSU) activists in connection with the alleged attack on former Health Minister Veena George at Kannur railway station cannot be sustained.
The SIT found that the protesters had not committed the offences alleged in the original chargesheet and stated that waving black flags as a form of protest did not constitute a criminal offence.

The final report was submitted by SIT chief U. Preman before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court in Kannur. The investigation team concluded that the protesters had not committed offences such as rioting, wrongful restraint, obstructing public servants from discharging their official duties or criminal trespass on railway premises.
The charge of attempted murder, which was initially included in the first information report, was subsequently dropped by the first investigation team while filing the chargesheet.

According to the SIT report, the responsibility of the police personnel accompanying Veena George was to prevent the protesters from approaching her. However, the protesters did not obstruct the police from discharging their official duties. Instead, the police stopped those waving black flags. The SIT also found that the Minister had not been wrongfully restrained by the protesters.

The report further stated that the protesters had entered the railway station after purchasing valid platform tickets. Therefore, the charge of trespassing on railway premises was not sustainable. The SIT also cited court observations that black flag protests did not constitute a criminal offence.

Meanwhile, the SIT had earlier submitted a separate report to the Director General of Police, recommending action against Veena George’s former gunman, Abhilash, for allegedly giving a false statement, as well as against officials who had allegedly failed to conduct the preliminary investigation properly.
The court will now decide on further proceedings based on the final report submitted by the SIT.

articles.title: Vigilance wing pulls up Kochi Metro Rail Limited over lapses in auctioning commercial spaces
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Vigilance wing of Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) has pulled up the agency for a slew of alleged omissions in the leasing of commercial spaces at the 22 metro stations along the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura phase-one corridor, which resulted in substantial revenue loss over the past few years.

The metro agency’s Vigilance wing observed that the auction of commercial spaces at the stations was conducted without advertisements and in a “less transparent” manner. The auctions were conducted outside the scope of the procurement manual, and the basic principles of transparency, competition, fairness and elimination of discretion were not followed in letter and spirit. Base rates were not fixed on the basis of objective data. Instead, a trial-and-error method was adopted.

Changes in rates and other conditions, such as the earnest money deposit (EMD), resulted in prospective bidders adopting a wait-and-see approach, while creating a sense of differential treatment among existing vendors. A level playing field was missing. Moreover, e-auction or forward auction through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) was not considered. In most cases, there was only a single bidder. The absence of a standard operating procedure for conducting auctions led to ad hoc practices and subjectivity in the process, further reflecting the lack of transparency.

The Vigilance wing also took note of the absence of a finance member in the auction committee, in contravention of the provisions of the procurement manual. There were also several corrections, overwritings and omissions in the registration forms and the auction register. Adding to the concerns, the terms and conditions of the auction were relaxed midway through the process without public notice. The EMD amount kept changing from one auction to another, and it was eventually decided not to collect it at all.

In view of these findings, the Vigilance wing recommended that base rates be fixed on the basis of objective data. It also called for a consistent policy on the auction of spaces for hiring or advertising to avoid the trial-and-error approach to fixing base rates, ambiguity in deciding the mode of auction and confusion over the auction procedure.

In this regard, a forward auction module of GeM or its e-auction module should be considered, after due preparation, instead of outdated and less transparent methods such as physical or hybrid auctions. Adequate publicity, including through the media, should be ensured to prevent ad hoc practices and subjectivity in conducting auctions. A standard operating procedure (SOP) for conducting auctions should be drawn up, and a finance member should be included in the auction committee. The mandatory declaration of ‘Conflict of Interest’ by auction committee members should also be ensured.
Other recommendations include continuous videographing or recording of the auction or tender process through CCTV and preparation of the minutes after the auction.

articles.title: BJP leaders criticise Mamata-Congress bonhomie
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leadership continued to criticise and raise questions about the bonhomie between the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress and the Congress party for the second consecutive day on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and accused the former Chief Minister of joining forces in Delhi to create anarchy in the country.

BJP president Nitin Nabin made a similar charge against Ms. Banerjee during a procession in Kolkata on Monday (November 2, 2026). On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and BJP leader and former Union Minister Smriti Irani criticised the coming together of the Mamata Banerjee and Congress party.

Mr. Adhikari, who participated in a ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ march at Siliguri in North Bengal, said that the former Chief Minister was not invited to inaugurate a single Durga Puja in Kolkata and that she is going to Delhi to ally with anarchists.

The Chief Minister tried to paint most of the Opposition parties that had assembled at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1 with the same brush, calling them dynasty parties and saying that they are four-generation, three-generation, and two-generation parties.

Mr. Adhikari referred to Congress as a “4G” party, referring to (Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, Rajiv Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi), Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) as “3G” (Karunanidhi, M.K. Stalin and Udhayanidhi Stalin), and Mamata Banerjee’s Trinamool Congress and Lalu Prasad Yadav Rashtriya Janata Dal as “2G” (Mamata Banerjee-Abhishek Banerjee and Lalu Prasad-Tejashwi Yadav). He added that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has “no G”.

BJP leader Smriti Irani, who held a press conference in Kolkata also spoke in a similar vein accusing the Trinamool Congress of trampling democracy in the State by unleashing attacks on BJP workers and committing atrocities on women workers. “Today those political goons are joining hands with the Congress at Ramlila Maidan,” she said. Ms. Irani called Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi as “perpetual prince in the waiting” and said that he is undermining the democratic institutions of the country.

The remarks by the BJP leadership come at a time when speculations are rife in the political circles about a larger Opposition unity taking place in the State. West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) called on all the Opposition parties to come together, keeping their flags aside and instead using “white flags”. Only a few weeks ago, Mamata Banerjee had decided to support Congress candidates in the Nandigram by-polls after her party’s nominee withdrew candidates at the last moment.

Reacting to the signs of new political alignment emerging, State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya called Mamata Banerjee, Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury and CPI(M) State Secretary Md. Salim to hold a procession “hand in hand”.

articles.title: Mobile phone, power banks seized from Kannur Central Jail
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A mobile phone and accessories, including two power banks, a charger and three data cables, were seized from Kannur Central Jail during a search by prison officials on Monday.

The prohibited articles were found hidden beneath stone slabs behind the jail’s second block. The Town police have registered a case and launched an investigation based on a complaint lodged by jail Joint Superintendent A. Shaiju.

The repeated seizure of prohibited articles from within the jail compound has raised concerns over security checks. Inadequate inspection of food items and cooking materials brought into the prison is suspected to be facilitating the smuggling of such articles.

articles.title: NMDC’s iron ore output rose 18% in Oct, sales dip amid rain impact
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: State-owned NMDC reported October iron ore production rose 18% year-on-year (YoY) to 5.04 million tonnes, while sales declined more than 11% to 3.44 MT.
For the seven months ended October, production stood at 32.32 MT (26.47 MT) and sales 25.67 MT (26.12 MT).

The company said dispatches were temporarily impacted by disruptions to the Kottavalasa–Kirandul (KK) railway line after sections of the route were washed away due to heavy monsoon rains in September and October. The disruption affected evacuation from NMDC’s Bailadila mines in Chhattisgarh for nearly a month.
With rail connectivity restored and supplies resumed, it expects the dispatches and sales to improve in the coming months, NMDC said.

“The 18% growth in iron ore production in October reflects the sustained efforts of the teams. With the rail connectivity restored and supplies resumed, we expect dispatches and sales to improve in the coming months,” CMD Amitava Mukherjee said. NMDC is eyeing 60 MT production this fiscal and becoming a 100 MT mining company by 2030.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia.
The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share.
The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year.
Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore.
The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year.
Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year.
Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year.

Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure.
“On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said.
The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end.
Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028.
He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier.

articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.
The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.
Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.
“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.
Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.
The government was now claiming to have secured a good deal by selling the bank at ₹81 a share, he said, demanding disclosure of both valuation reports and the identity of the second bidder.

Mr. Gohil invoked an assurance given by the then Finance Minister Jaswant Singh in Parliament in August 2003 that the government’s stake in IDBI Bank would not be reduced below 51%. A Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance had also favoured retaining the government’s majority stake, he said.

He further questioned the regulatory concessions extended to Fairfax, including the two-year window reportedly allowed to reduce its control in another Indian bank, and sought details of the source of funds for the acquisition.

articles.title: Capex push to continue, but fiscal prudence non-negotiable: FM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to sustaining capital expenditure (capex) to support economic growth, while stressing that fiscal prudence would remain non-negotiable.

“Capex is a very important component of our growth strategy. Because till such time the private sector will be able to expand capacity or make capital investment, it is important for the Government to push through with capital investment,” she said at an event organised by HSBC India in Mumbai.
Pointing to the returns from public investment over the past four to five years, she said the multiplier effects had strengthened the Government’s confidence in continuing the spending push.

“We find that in the last 4 to 5 years, we have got very good success. The multipliers actually work and it gives us confidence that the Government is not going to sit back and watch whether growth is growing without doing much,” she said.

The Government would be willing to extend capex support to ensure that the growth momentum was not disrupted. “We will continue doing that because India’s growth momentum should not be lost at all,” she said.
However, Ms. Sitharaman made it clear that higher public spending would have to be balanced against fiscal constraints.
“We need to be fiscally prudent,” she said, adding that while some advocated spending without worrying about sovereign credit ratings, responsible expenditure was essential.
“I agree we need to spend but it has to be done responsibly and fiscal prudence will be our top priority,” she emphasised.
“We have to be prudent and we have to be creative based on which we can encourage growth and stability,” she added.
The Finance Minister also called for greater confidence in India’s economic prospects, urging businesses and experts to move beyond pessimism and sector-specific concerns.

“India must to talk with optimism and there needs to be reduction in cynicism,” she said, questioning why experts who considered their own sectors healthy remained apprehensive about the broader economy.
“If your sector doing fine, others sectors in India must be similarly fine. So can the narrate and language change?” she asked.

articles.title: No-cost EMI: a loan that is portrayed as free
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Every festive season, the same board greets you at the electronics shop: “No-cost EMI”. TVs, washing machines and appliances are available at no-cost EMI. A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays. Lets see who.

A bank or finance firm funds the purchase and charges interest. The shop agrees to bear interest but it will recover it in one of two ways. Either the price quoted to you is higher, or you lose the discount a cash buyer would have got Take the same phone. A cash buyer gets it for ₹57,000. The EMI buyer pays ₹60,000. The ₹3,000 gap is the interest.

articles.title: Top UN court to rule November 19 on Rohingya genocide case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The top United Nations court will on November 19 deliver a landmark ruling on whether Myanmar’s crackdown against its mostly Muslim Rohingya minority constituted a genocide , officials said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Judges at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) have for seven years been weighing accusations by The Gambia that Myanmar’s brutal repression of the Rohingya breached the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.

While the ICJ has no means of enforcing its decisions, a ruling that Myanmar committed genocide would heap more international pressure on its military junta and be seen as justice for hundreds of thousands of Rohingya.

Legal experts are closely watching the decision from the ICJ, which rules in disputes between countries, for clues as to how the court might sway in the seminal genocide case brought by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.

Myanmar has always denied carrying out a genocide against the Rohingya, arguing its actions targeted a military uprising from insurgents after a series of attacks left a dozen security personnel dead.

The crackdown by the Myanmar army and Buddhist militias forced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh, bringing with them harrowing accounts of gang rape and mass executions.
More than one million Rohingya still live across the border in Bangladesh, in the world’s largest refugee settlement.
During hearings on the case in January, Gambian Justice Minister Dawda Jallow told the court the Rohingya had suffered “the most horrific violence and destruction one could imagine”.
“It is not about esoteric issues of international law. It is about real people, real stories and a real group of human beings,” said Mr. Jallow.
“The Rohingya of Myanmar. They have been targeted for destruction,” added the Minister.
The Gambia has brought the case to the ICJ under the terms of the UN Genocide Convention, which allows any state to sound the alarm if it suspects genocide is being committed.
The alleged violations of the convention “are a stain on our collective conscience and it would be irresponsible to pretend that it is not our business,” Mr. Jallow said.

articles.title: Trump says U.S. cutting $3.8 billion annual security assistance to Israel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that Washington is ending a 10-year security assistance accord with Israel that allowed $3.8 billion in annual assistance to its ally until 2028.
Mr. Trump said Israel was “fine” with him ending the assistance, which began in 2019 and was signed under his predecessor, Barack Obama, three years earlier.
“We’ll help Israel if they need it,” Mr. Trump added in an interview on “Fox and Friends,” saying that he had agreed with Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cut the assistance.
“Israel’s our number one; we give them more than anybody else, and they no longer need it... If they did need it, I would say keep it going,” Mr. Trump added.
Under the deal, Israel receives financial assistance for the purchase of around $3.8 billion in weapons a year.

Since its founding in 1948, Israel has received more than $300 billion, adjusted for inflation, in U.S. economic and military assistance, according to the Council on Foreign Relations, far more than any other country since 1946.
The Israeli premier has said he wanted to end Israel’s reliance on U.S. support.
In June, Mr. Netanyahu called for his country to increase its military autonomy and reduce its reliance on Washington.
In January, he told The Economist that he hoped to do so within a decade, while in May he told CBS that he wanted support to reach “zero”.
Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) announcement was nonetheless met with backlash from Israeli opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot, who said it showed that Mr. Netanyahu must go.

“The fact that Israel’s defense establishment is learning of a shift in our strategic relationship through the media, at the same time as the Israeli public, shows just how dangerous Benjamin Netanyahu’s conduct is,” Mr. Eisenkot said in a statement.

On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), Mr. Trump cited attacks by leftist Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for the U.S. Senate in Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) midterm elections after harnessing popular discontent and anti-Israel sentiment, as part of the reasoning behind the decision to end aid.

articles.title: U.S. Midterm Elections 2026 LIVE: Trump says midterm results will be ‘better than you think’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: In the hours before polls opened for the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday, federal judges issued a series of rulings restricting the Trump administration’s unprecedented efforts to pressure state election ⁠officials over alleged noncitizen voting.

Over the past several months, as President Donald Trump’s fellow Republicans geared up to defend their majorities in both houses of Congress, the administration ramped up a crackdown on noncitizen voting, which Mr. Trump allies say is a ‌major problem even though evidence suggests it is exceedingly rare.

That push has repeatedly encountered resistance in the courts. Federal judges have found that the Trump administration was overstepping its authority by ‌wading into election administration, a responsibility that the U.S. Constitution assigns to the states, and that ‌lists ⁠it had generated of alleged noncitizens registered to vote were inaccurate and risked disenfranchising naturalised U.S. ⁠citizens.

Ballot machines malfunctioned in a hotly contested House race in New York state Tuesday, prompting right-wing influencers to fling unfounded allegations of U.S. midterms voter fraud even as local election officials insisted all ballots would be counted.
President Donald Trump and his allies have previously spread unproven claims about voting machines, alleging that they are faulty or unreliable.
The Westchester County Board of Elections said it was aware of an issue involving paper ballots that is preventing voting machines from accepting ballots at polling locations throughout the county.
The board “wants to reassure every voter that your vote matters, your ballot will be secure and your vote will be counted,” with ballots instead placed in emergency bags, it said in a statement.

On polling day, Donald Trump sprung a surprise by announcing that the U.S. will stop providing Israel USD four billion in aid from next year, which Democrat Ro Khanna described as a desperate attempt to stave off a “Blue tsunami”.
On the eve of the elections, the U.S. launched limited strikes on Iran’s Qesham island in the Hormuz Strait. Officials said that the strikes were in response to Iran firing at a U.S. aircraft.

U.S. rock legend Bruce Springsteen, a staunch Democrat, urged election officials Tuesday to resist any government voting interference amid fears President Donald Trump’s administration may intervene in the midterms.

“I’m speaking to election officials and representatives of our government on election day. You have sworn an oath to preserve, protect and defend our Constitution,” the 77-year-old said in a video on Instagram.

“That means you have a solemn duty to ensure that our votes are securely counted,” he said. “You who represent us must never consent to any directives that undermine our constitutional right to a free and fair election.”

articles.title: Iran president says return to war benefits 'no one', after reported U.S. strikes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that a return to war would benefit "no one", hours after reported U.S. strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.
It came as U.S. voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump's grip on power.

Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the U.S., Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Islamic republic was "ready for battle with its finger on the trigger", while deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran retained the right to "legitimate self-defence" after the strikes.

But Mr. Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue", adding that "no one will benefit from this war" if it reignited, and emphasising that the country's supreme leader had recently granted the government new powers to negotiate issues previously "off-limits".

The U.S. strikes, reported by The Wall Street Journal, CNN, The New York Times and other outlets, hit Qeshm island in the Hormuz waterway, a key flashpoint of the Middle East war that has upended global markets.
Unnamed U.S. officials cited by the outlets described the attacks as defensive in nature. The Journal said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes.
U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.
The U.S. and Israel launched their war with Iran with a massive wave of strikes in late February. The conflict has been stalemated for months.
Asked if Israel was involved in the latest reported strikes, an Israeli military spokesperson told AFP , "No".

The reported Qeshm attack came just hours after Mr. Trump signalled a deal with Iran "could happen", as U.S. voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterms dominated by public dissatisfaction with the war and the inflation it has brought.
"Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible," Mr. Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.
Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies.

articles.title: Death toll hits 31 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with dozens still missing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 31 on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), with dozens of people still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people.

Teams of rescuers and volunteers continued to search the cratered blast site of a destroyed aid facility and shelter in Komyushuvakha, a village in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region, hoping to find more than 45 missing residents alive under the rubble. Instead, more bodies were pulled out and carried away in white plastic sheeting.

“The scale of the tragedy is terrifying,” Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the region's military administration, wrote in an online post. “This is one of the worst tragedies in terms of the number of civilian victims in our region since the start of the full-scale war.”

Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.

“The Russians think America won't notice this signal of theirs,” he said. “But we need to notice and stop such terror. We need to help Ukraine defend its skies; otherwise, Russia will never stop its missile strikes.”
Three days of mourning were declared in Zaporizhzhia, where Russian bunker-busting bombs, filled with nearly 1.5 tons of explosives, were used in Monday's (November 2) attack.
The dead included four police officers and two rescue workers, Mr. Semikin said on Tuesday (November 3). At least five people were hurt.
In the northeast region of Kharkiv, a combined Russian missile and drone attack wounded at least 62 people, local authorities said.

A strike damaged a medical facility in the Nemyshlianskyi district, shattered windows in four apartment buildings and damaged cars. More than 200 patients were transferred to other medical facilities, head of the regional military administration Oleh Syniehubov said.
In the Dnipro area, rescuers pulled a woman alive from the rubble on Tuesday (November 3) morning, after a Russian attack killed one person and wounded 17, local authorities said.
The attack damaged an outpatient clinic and a hospital. Patients were transferred to other hospitals, Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said.

Moscow kept up its nightly attacks on power plants and energy infrastructure ahead of winter, causing extensive damage and electricity outages as it carried out 20 strikes in 10 regions overnight, Ukraine's energy ministry said.

articles.title: U.S. Midterm Election night agenda: When polls close and when to expect results
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: With voters deciding thousands of races across the United States on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), keeping track of the contests to watch and when results may arrive can be tricky.
Here is a rundown of the major races, hour by hour, and an indication of how long vote-counting may take.

The first polls of the night close in most of Indiana and Kentucky, but statewide winners will not be declared in either state until the last polls close at 7 p.m. (5.30 a.m. IST, November 4, 2026) . Winners could be declared in the States’ easternmost congressional districts.
Key contests include competitive U.S. House races in Indiana’s 5th and Kentucky’s 6th congressional districts.

7 p.m. (5.30 a.m. IST): .All polls close in six States, including Georgia, South Carolina and Virginia, which typically complete most of their vote counting on election night. In the 2024 general election, vote counting in all three States reached the halfway mark during the 8 p.m. hour.

The counts were 90% complete at 10.21 p.m. (8:51 a.m. IST) in Georgia, 11.14 p.m. (9:44 a.m. IST) in South Carolina and 12.07 a.m. (10.37 a.m. IST) in Virginia. The Associated Press declared Republican Donald Trump the winner of Georgia’s competitive presidential contest at 12.58 a.m. (11.28 a.m. IST).

Most Florida polls also close at 7 p.m. (5.30 a.m. IST), including those in every competitive congressional district. Statewide winners will not be declared until polls close in the Central Time Zone at 8 p.m. (6.30 a.m. IST)

7.30 p.m. (6 a.m. IST): Polls close in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia. All three States counted votes relatively quickly in 2024, reaching the halfway point at about 7.30 a.m. and roughly 90% by the 9.30 a.m. hour. The AP declared a winner in Ohio’s competitive 2024 U.S. Senate race at 11.27 p.m. (9.57 a.m. IST)

Key contests include U.S. Senate races in Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio; gubernatorial races in Georgia and Ohio; and U.S. House races in Florida, Indiana, South Carolina, Virginia, Ohio and North Carolina.
8 p.m. hour (6.30 a.m. IST): This is prime time on election night, with polls fully or partially closing in nearly half the States, including Florida, Maine, New Hampshire and Pennsylvania.

Florida typically counts votes quickly, with results from much of the State beginning to come in during the 7 p.m. hour (5:30 a.m. IST). In 2024, 90% of the vote had been counted by 8.07 p.m. (6.37 a.m. IST)

In 2024, vote counts in New Hampshire and Pennsylvania reached the halfway mark at 10.12 p.m. (8.42 a.m. IST). They reached 90% at 12.48 a.m. (11.18 a.m. IST) in Pennsylvania and 1:42 a.m. (12.12 p.m. IST) in New Hampshire. Maine did not reach the halfway mark until 12.54 a.m. (11.24 a.m. IST)

articles.title: West Bengal's first relocated tigress captured on sojourn in Assam, returned to Buxa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The three-year-old tigress, who was recently relocated to West Bengal 's Buxa Tiger Reserve from Bihar , was captured on a foray into Assam and returned to West Bengal on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

The tigress, Dooars Rani (BTR-TF-1/ T-138), was released in Buxa on October 2 from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve as part of the State’s first tiger relocation project. She crossed into Assam's Raimona National Park on Sunday (October 25, 2026) in search of habitat.

"On Tuesday, we tranquilised the tigress, caged her, and brought her back to Buxa. Initially we let her explore and captured her today only when she came close to human settlements. However, there is nothing to panic about now. The tigress is also safe and healthy," said Forest Minister Manoj Oraon. The minister has been present in Assam for the last four days to monitor the tigress.

According to the officials, the tigress crossed the Sankosh River and a road in Gosaigaon in Assam to enter Raimona looking for habitat. Her movement area was traced up to 25 km from the Bengal border.

Forest officials from Assam and West Bengal, along with a team from the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), initially decided to let her explore. "She is not the property of any government. It is the nature of tigers to explore. She will likely cross into Raimona or any other area again. Our team will continue to monitor her," said the minister.

On October 2, the tigress was translocated from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve and released in the presence of Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. The CM said three more tigers would be released in Buxa over the next two months, and the initiative would not only help in conservation but also in boosting tourism.

Buxa was declared a tiger reserve in 1983, but there have been no reports of a tiger’s presence in the region of late. According to an official statement by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the recovery of Buxa has been a sustained, science-based effort, and the Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Project, initiated by the Government of West Bengal with support from the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), has been implemented collaboratively since 2018.

Forest officials say this new tigress from Bihar will be subjected to intensive post-release monitoring using a combination of telemetry, camera trapping, and field-based monitoring to assess her movement, adaptation, health, and behaviour.

articles.title: Mexico bans cellphones in schools, despite opposition from parents worried about violence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Starting Tuesday, Mexican schools will ban cellphones from classrooms as part of a federal government effort to limit children's and teenagers' use of electronic devices, following similar measures taken by over a hundred countries in the last decade.

The initiative, spearheaded by Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, has been supported by experts who see it as an opportunity to reduce young Mexicans' exposure to technology and the resulting attention deficit, stress and anxiety.

Mexican authorities are also preparing to implement regulations this month that will require digital platforms to remove posts containing hate speech, abuse, sexual violence, harassment, cyberbullying and other illegal content.

However, the cellphone ban, which will take effect on November 3, is already facing resistance in some parts of the country. Some parents fear being unable to communicate with their children amid ongoing violence, from which children and adolescents are not spared.

According to the civil society coalition Network for Children's Rights in Mexico (REDIM), in the first half of this year, one in 10 Mexicans between the ages of 0 and 17 were victims of crimes involving organised crime.

“I don't think parents will accept not giving their children a means of digital communication, especially when those children … are spending so much time at home instead of at school,” said Francisco Ortiz, state representative of the National Union of Parents in Sinaloa, accusing the government of ignoring parents and approving regulations that “go against parental authority, against the rights of parents.”

The decree issued by Sheinbaum prohibits the use of cellphones and electronic devices inside elementary and middle schools throughout the school day, and only allows their use for educational purposes under the guidance of teachers or for personal emergencies, disability and health needs. Students can take their phones with them on the way to school.

Benigno Gomez, a father from Reynosa in the northern state of Tamaulipas, said that while he understood the educational authorities' need to reduce students' time on cellphones, he found it “a little difficult” that they weren't allowed to have a cellphone to deal with a potential risk situation.
Mexican authorities have not commented on these concerns and have instead focused on the harm caused by cellphones.

During a recent address to the Chamber of Deputies, Mexico's Secretary of Public Education, Mario Delgado, stated that the Sheinbaum administration seeks to “prevent addiction to digital platforms and the disorders they cause in minors.”

Just as the sun was beginning to rise, the residents of Escuinapa, the capital of the municipality of the same name located in southern Sinaloa, awoke on the morning of October 22 to alarming news. A bus that regularly travels through the small town -- which relies on mango and shrimp production -- was shot at by a man on a motorcycle.

More than a dozen high school students were on board. A video recorded by one of the passengers circulated on social media, showing children on the floor and others hiding among the seats while one teenager asks another, “Do you have any credit (on your cellphone)?”

What followed, over the course of just about 20 minutes, was the biggest crypto hack in history, with more than $6 billion worth being stolen. By November 2, Binance had replaced 100% of the stolen amount to customers. The search for the culprit and recovery process still continues, but the customer impact has been mitigated in a remarkably short time.

Cryptocurrency transactions involve a multi-rung authentication involving public keys as well as private keys that are held by each user. articles.title: Approval of India-made version of HIV-prevention shot raises hopes in low-income countries
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved an India-made generic version of the world's only twice-a-year shot to prevent HIV -- a big step toward making the drug available inexpensively and more quickly in 120 low- and middle-income countries.
The announcement was made on Monday morning by the manufacturer and organisations that helped to speed up development of the medication, called lenacapavir.

The generic was developed by India-based Dr. Reddy's Laboratories under an agreement brokered by Unitaid, the Clinton Health Access Initiative and Wits RHI, a health research institute in Africa. The partners sought to accelerate development and make the drug available at an affordable price.

The drug is expected to cost USD 40 a year per person in the countries where it will be available, the same price as daily preventive pills available now. But the shots are much more convenient than the pills because they're needed much less frequently and they nearly eliminated new infections in two groundbreaking studies of people at high risk.

People don't always take their daily dose of medication, “and if you do not take it, you cannot get protected against HIV,” said Carmen Perez Casas, HIV lead for the grant-making organisation Unitaid, a global health agency. “With lenacapavir, we are much more hopeful.”

Ultimately, advocates said, the medication should help drive down cases of HIV and AIDS -- and deaths. According to the WHO, 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV and 570,000 died from HIV-related causes last year.

With an affordable, high-quality generic medication now available, “we could help to scale this to the 20 million people around the world who need PrEP,” prescription medicine taken by people at risk of HIV before being exposed to the virus, said Carolyn Amole, who leads the HIV programme for the Clinton Health Access Initiative, a global health organisation.
“And if we scale to those levels,” she added, “we can actually begin to bring an end to the HIV epidemic.”

Generic lenacapavir can't be sold in the U.S. because a brand-name version, Yeztugo, made by Gilead Sciences and approved last year, is still protected by a patent. The U.S. list price for that version, meaning the cost before insurance, is USD 28,218 a year. Gilead officials say that's similar to some other types of PrEP, which stands for pre-exposure prophylaxis.

The new generic was approved by the FDA under a longstanding practice designed to ensure the quality of HIV-related drugs provided to other countries by the U.S. government. Approval of a drug by the U.S. FDA can speed regulatory approval in many other countries. The approval is considered “tentative,” the FDA's standard designation for generics while the originator remains under patent.

Until now, Gilead has been the sole supplier of lenacapavir, and demand has outstripped supply in low- and middle-income countries. Last year, Gilead established royalty-free licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers to enable production. Those voluntary licenses cover a specific set of countries in sub-Saharan Africa, Asia and Latin America.

“We share the sense of urgency around expanding access to lenacapavir for HIV prevention,” a Gilead spokesperson said in a statement. “We believe we have enabled the fastest and most sustainable path to expanding access for communities most affected by HIV.”

articles.title: WHO urged to review drinking water standards amid nitrate health fears
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Dozens of global health and environmental organisations called on the World Health Organization on Tuesday to revise decades-old standards for nitrate levels in drinking water, arguing they do not reflect recent scientific evidence about potential health risks.

In an open letter, 85 organisations, including Greenpeace International and the World Organization of Family Doctors (WONCA), called on the United Nations health agency to include nitrate in an upcoming review of its drinking water guidelines.
The toxic effects of nitrates -- a residue left behind by intensive farming -- are widely recognised as particularly dangerous for children and pregnant women.

But the current WHO guidelines -- which set the maximum acceptable nitrate level in drinking water at 50 milligrammes per litre as nitrate or 11.3 milligrammes per litre as nitrate-nitrogen -- date back to 1958 and are "outdated", the organisations warned.
That level was set specifically to prevent so-called "blue-baby syndrome" -- a deadly blood disorder in which the blood's capacity for carrying oxygen is reduced.

But the limit "has not been updated in response to robust epidemiological evidence linking chronic, low-level nitrate exposure to long-term human health risks", Tuesday's letter said, pointing in particular to "colorectal cancer and adverse birth outcomes".
"Studies now link nitrate in drinking water, at levels well below the current WHO limit, to bowel cancer and premature birth," WONCA chair Pratyush Kumar said in a joint statement.
The letter was sent to coincide with WHO's annual One Health Day, which aims to raise awareness about the interconnected health of humans, animals, plants and shared ecosystems.
Surface water models indicate that hundreds of millions of people globally are exposed to elevated nitrate levels, the letter warned.
"Water should be life-giving, not life-threatening," Amanda Larsson, the global project lead for agriculture at Greenpeace, said in the statement.
"We cannot protect human health without protecting the groundwater and rivers that sustain us," she insisted.

"Governments must take decisive action to curb the growth of intensive livestock farming and actively support producers in transitioning to ecological farming practices -- ensuring that clean, safe drinking water isn't a luxury but a guarantee."

articles.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

articles.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 28, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Iranian woman moves Madras High Court wanting to know procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous visa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 30-year-old Iranian woman, reportedly born in a Zoroastrian family but forced to practice Islam in her country before converting to Christianity, has approached the Madras High Court seeking a direction to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Chennai to explain to her the procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous Visa so that she could step out of a special camp for foreigners in Tiruchi.

Pegah Ansari, daughter of Ansari Shapour, told the court that she was born and raised in a Zoroastrian family in Tehran. Claiming that all citizens at birth get registered as Muslims, irrespective of their actual religious background or personal faith, in her country; the petitioner said: “As a result, despite being born into a Zoroastrian family, I was officially recorded as a Muslim in government records.”

She went on to state: “Throughout my life in Iran, I lived under constant fear of persecution on account of my religious beliefs and personal convictions. Over time, I came to believe in and follow the teachings of Christianity. Due to the strict restrictions imposed on religious conversion in Iran, I was compelled to practice and profess my Christian faith only in private and in secrecy.”

Ms. Ansari said, she had no other option but to flee her country in 2019 because her private conversion to Christianity came to the notice of the authorities in Iran where she faced a genuine and imminent threat of persecution, harassment and possible arrest. She flew first to Georgia and underwent conversion through appropriate religious process. She resided there till 2022.

Her second stop was Sri Lanka where stayed approximately for a month before flying down to India on a one-month-long tourist visa in April 2022. “I came to India in search of safety, stability, and the freedom to live without fear of religious persecution,” the petitioner said and claimed to have obtained refugee status from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in March 2025.

She said, the Anjugramam police in Kanniyakumari district had arrested her on December 10, 2025 when she had gone to a resort over there for decorating the venue of a birthday party. The charge levelled against her was that she had overstayed in India despite the expiry of her tourist visa on May 12, 2022. The police personnel also found that the petitioner’s Iranian passport had expired on February 17, 2024.

The petitioner was lodged at the women’s prison at Puzhal near Chennai until the Kanniyakumari Principal District and Sessions Court granted her bail on January 29, 2026. Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to the Tiruchi special camp for foreigners on the basis of a December 23, 2025 Government Order which authorised her detention in the camp until the disposal of the criminal case or her deportation.

Claiming that the State could not curtail her free movement even after grant of bail, the petitioner said, she would be able to approach the appropriate authorities for getting relocated to some other country only if she was allowed to move freely without being confined to the boundaries of the special camp. The petitioner wanted to know the procedure for obtaining the visa required to face court proceedings.
The petitioner said that she had made a representation in this regard to the FRRO on June 25, 2026 but complained that the officer did not respond.
